newsitem.title: INDIA: Heavy rains claim 29 lives in south India.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rains claim 29 lives in south India.

text.p: Torrential rains have killed at least 29 people and made thousands homeless over the weekend in the southern Indian states of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, officials said.

Officials in Andhra Pradesh, where at least 19 people have died, said life had come to a standstill in many parts of the state as thousands of mud houses collapsed and crops were destroyed in the steady downpour.

Chandrababu Naidu, chief minister of Andhra Pradesh said rescue operations were being carried out by army helicopters with people airlifted from the flood-affected coastal areas of Cuddapah and Prakasam districts.
"The majority of deaths in the monsoon season occurred predominantly due to the collapse of houses and electrocution caused by rains and floods," said an agriculture ministry expert.

Officials in Tamil Nadu's capital city of Madras said non-stop rain for two hours on Friday dumped more than five inches (14 cm) of water in the city and damaged 45,000 huts in the low lying coastal areas.
The downpour marked the begining of the northeast monsoon rains, officials said.
The losses in land and property are still being estimated.
